games.title: Greater, Less, Equal
games.blurb: Comparing numbers, sums and measures
games.intro: Let’s compare! The “greater than” and “less than” sign looks like a bird’s beak: it is always open toward the bigger number. And if both sides are the same, we put “equals”.

samples.prompt: Compare 5 and 9. Which sign goes between them?
Compare 2 plus 6 and 8. Which sign goes between them?

What time is it on the clock?

games.title: Story Problems
games.blurb: Stories from life: the shop, friends, the road
games.intro: Listen to a little story and answer the question. The pictures show what we know and what is asked. If you need to, tap the speaker and I will read the problem again.

samples.prompt: There were 2 birds sitting on the branch. Then 3 more flew in. How many birds are on the branch now?
One notebook costs 7 dollars. How many dollars do 5 notebooks cost?
Victor bought 2 cupcakes for 3 dollars each and tea for 14 dollars. How many dollars did he pay?

games.title: Guess the Flag
games.blurb: All 192 flags of the world — starting with the best known
games.intro: Every country has a flag of its own. Listen to the name of the country and find its flag among six! On every step there are five new flags, and the ones you know come back so that you don’t forget them.

samples.prompt: Find the flag of the United States.
Find the flag of Montenegro.
Find the flag of Micronesia.

games.title: Put the Map Together
games.blurb: Put animals and flags on the continents
games.intro: There are seven continents on Earth. Drag the animal or the flag onto the continent where it belongs.

samples.prompt: Where does the lion live? Drag it onto the map.
Which continent is Czechia on? Drag the flag.
Which continent is Pakistan on? Drag the flag.

games.title: Animals and Natural Zones
games.blurb: 82 animals and seven natural zones — from the Arctic to the savanna
games.intro: Every animal loves its own home. Some are happy among the ice, and some in the hot desert. Help them get home! Farther along the way there are new animals, “Who is it?” riddles and “Who is the odd one out?” puzzles.

samples.prompt: Where does the polar bear live?
Who is it? A bird that spreads its tail into a huge colorful fan.
Who is the odd one out? All the others are neighbors: they live in the same natural zone.

games.title: Seas and Oceans
games.blurb: Five oceans, half a hundred seas and gulfs, islands, countries and rivers
games.intro: There are five oceans on our planet. Listen to where to sail, and tap the right ocean on the map! Farther along the way there are riddles about oceans, seas and gulfs, islands, countries and rivers.

samples.prompt: Sail to the Indian Ocean!
Around which ocean does the “Ring of Fire” of volcanoes run? Sail there!
Which ocean washes the shores of Somalia? Sail there!

games.title: Capitals
games.blurb: 80 capitals of the world, their famous buildings and fun facts
games.intro: Know a capital by its most famous building and by the name of its country. Every step brings new capitals, and the ones you know come back so that you don’t forget them!

samples.prompt: What is the capital of Japan?
What is the capital of the United Arab Emirates?
Quito is the capital of which country?

games.title: Day, Night and Time Difference
games.blurb: Why it is day in some cities when it is night in others, and what time it is there
games.intro: The Earth turns, and the Sun lights up first one side of it, then the other. So when it is day here, somewhere far away it is night. Let’s find out where it is day and where it is night, and what time it is in cities around the world!

samples.prompt: It is night in Kyiv now. What about Los Angeles?
It is 14:00 in Kyiv. It is 1 hour earlier in Warsaw than in Kyiv. What time is it in Warsaw?
It is 7:00 in Kyiv. In winter it is 7 hours later in Tokyo than in Kyiv. What time is it in Tokyo?

games.title: Eco Patrol
games.blurb: Sorting rubbish: a hundred things — glass, paper, plastic, metal and compost

samples.prompt: Which bin is right for the glass oil bottle?
Which bin is right for the piece of wire?

games.title: Why Is That?
games.blurb: Why glaciers melt and why fallen leaves must not be burned
games.intro: Nature needs our help. Listen to the question and choose the answer — and I will tell you why it matters: about air, water, animals, rubbish and warmth on the planet.

samples.prompt: Why do we make bird feeders in winter?
samples.right: It is hard for birds to find food under the snow

samples.prompt: How do house plants help at home?
What is done at a recycling plant?
samples.right: Rubbish is sorted and turned into raw material

samples.prompt: Drawings in a cave — when was that?
